sentences.text: Sorry I’m late.
That’s OK. So, what have you found out while we have been waiting?
Well, it seems to have a big exhibition about the great human migration from Africa.
It’s on for another few weeks, until the end of April.
Sounds good. So, how much does it cost?
Well, it’s only 50 to enter.
I bought us two tickets already.
Oh, OK. I’ll give you the money later.
What else did you find out?
Well, it’s close on Mondays.
Oh, and importantly, we can’t take photos.
OK, let me make a note of all this.
I’ve brought my iPad.
OK, so you say we can’t go on Mondays or take photos.
Right. OK, but I agree, is a really interesting topic.
And 50 seems very reasonable.
Plus, if it’s on until April 30th that’s perfect for our field trip.
OK, we can go and check it out.
Great. OK, so where are we now?
Right, so, we’re standing in the Great Hall Oh, look: there’s the exhibition on the great human migration.
You see? There, next to the exhibition on early transportation.
Where? Opposite the Egyptian Room?
What? No, no.
On the other side.
Where do you see it?
I still can’t see it.
There. Look. See the sign.
Ah, OK. I see it now Right, well, let’s go and have a look.
Have you got my ticket?
Here you are.
OK, this looks great.
Where do we start?
Look over here.
Wow, it says that early modern humans lived in Africa for a really long time.
Then around 70 ,000 years ago they began to migrate from Africa.
Right, so, apparently, they started in Africa and then they started started to move to other continents, and all this happened 17 ,000 years ago!
And how do you think they traveled?
There were no cars or aeroplanes back then!
Well, it says here they traveled mostly on foot to reach Asia.
They needed to use canoes to cross the water to Australia.
Yeah, but what routes did they take?
I mean, how did they actually get to Australia?
It’s such a long way.
Good question. Well it says here they got there in stages by going from island to island.
Oh, I see.
So, they used they can use to travel from island to island before reaching Australia.
Right, and presumably they did the same going from Asia to America.
Or maybe they just swam?
no Look at this part of the map.
You see? early Early humans reached America on foot, using a land bridge from Asia during the Ice Age.
Now the ice has melted, the bridge has disappeared.
I’m noting this down.
So, they used can news from island to island to get to Australia, and walked across a land bridge to get to the American continent.
Interesting! Right? Now we know where these early migrants came from and more or less when it happened, but we still don’t know why they chose to move away from their homes in Africa.
Look, the display next to the map might help.
It's sad that possible reasons for migration include lack of food or fighting with other humans.
Uh, I see, so they needed to move to find food and escape from other humans who they were fighting with.
Yeah. Right, let’s have a look at the last bit of this exhibit.
exhibit. It looks like it’s about some of the effects of the great migration and what humans learn to do.
Look at this display here about how humans adapted to their new environments.
You know, by clothing themselves, designing weapons for hunting, building homes, and learning how to farm for food.
Yeah, this is all amazing.
I mean, we have never learned about any of this in school.
Yeah, I know.
